newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch sees Fin Min/Treasurer split enduring.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch sees Fin Min/Treasurer split enduring.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Tuesday the creation of two major finance roles in the New Zealand government was likely to be a long-lasting development.

The Coalition Agreement reached in December between the incumbent National Party and the nationalist New Zealand First party gave Birch the junior finance role, while NZ First leader Winston Peters took the new, senior finance title of Treasurer.

"The separation of roles, justified on grounds of workload alone, is, in my view, likely to become a permanent part of the political landscape in New Zealand," Birch told a business breakfast meeting in Wellington.

"The protocols we have signed may therefore come to have significance beyond the term of the present parliament, as a constitutional foundation for relations between the two offices, on a long-term basis," he said.

Birch said the new government had been born in a climate of "quite silly cynicism" fostered in part by media new to the Mixed Member Proportional voting system, and also by left-wing parties squirming after defeat at the hands of voters.

"If you look objectively at its programme, however, you have to conclude that this coalition has more to offer than National or New Zealand First did singly, and vastly more than any rival left-wing coalition."
Birch said there would inevitably be tensions between the two parties, but properly managed those tensions could be a source of strength.
